selected_problem: Fresh canonical main already validated persisted postimage bytes before apply and preimage bytes before rollback, but apply itself did not prove that before.contentBase64/before.size/before.sha256 remained self-consistent before performing workspace side effects. A staged changeset with a corrupted durable preimage could therefore be applied successfully and only become non-reversible when rollback later rejected the same corrupted preimage.
decision_basis: The repository already defines before.contentBase64/before.size/before.sha256 as one transactional preimage and already provides stagedBeforeBytes(change) to verify that invariant during rollback.
Reusing the same verifier during apply preflight closes an existing reversibility invariant without selecting a new trust model, product architecture, interface, or development order.

Hosted Developer Execution Runtime remained temporarily unavailable with HTTP 502, so this cycle used DWAC_SOURCE_CONTRACT_REPLAY（DWAC 源码契约重放） plus exact local focused validation and does not claim hosted execution success.

pre_fix_reality.focused_reproduction: EXPECTED_FAILURE: 1/2 PASS, 1/2 FAIL with Missing expected exception; apply accepted a persisted preimage whose contentBase64 no longer matched its recorded hash and changed the workspace.
pre_fix_reality.impact: A changeset could cross from STAGED to APPLIED even though its durable rollback preimage was already corrupt, weakening the repository's reversible changeset guarantee.

change: Apply preflight now executes stagedBeforeBytes(change) before validating the postimage and before any workspace write/delete. A corrupt persisted preimage therefore fails closed while the workspace still matches the original pre-apply state.

validation.node_check: PASS on the exact proposed core/changesets.mjs content
validation.intact_roundtrip: PASS: an intact persisted preimage still permits apply followed by exact rollback

truth_boundary: This proves internal self-consistency of the persisted preimage before apply side effects. It is not an authenticated signature or external trust root and does not protect against a coherent rewrite of the complete changeset and all matching metadata.
